```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(easyNIS)
```

## Attach the annual cost-to-charge ratios

Keep the CCR file for each year alongside its matching NIS release. Read the
CCR file documentation for the hospital key and ratio to use, then assemble
one table with `YEAR`, `HOSP_NIS`, and the chosen ratio named `CCR_NIS`.
Hospital identifiers can repeat across years. Record the source release and
ratio field for each year.

| Input | Annual link to Core | How to attach it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Hospital characteristics | `YEAR`, `HOSP_NIS` | `nis_join_companion(..., component = "hospital")` |
| Severity measures | `YEAR`, `KEY_NIS` | `nis_join_companion(..., component = "severity")` |
| Cost-to-charge ratios | `YEAR`, `HOSP_NIS` | Attach the separately prepared CCR table |

The companion helper validates keys and requires a companion file for each
opened year. A Core row with no matching companion key gets missing values.
The CCR example projects only the fields needed for an in-memory cost
calculation. The invented ratio table intentionally omits 2020.

```{r ccr-link}
charges <- nis_open(nis_example(years = 2018:2020)) |>
  dplyr::select(YEAR, HOSP_NIS, TOTCHG) |>
  dplyr::collect()
ccr <- data.frame(
  YEAR = rep(c(2018L, 2019L), each = 12L),
  HOSP_NIS = rep(1:12, times = 2L),
  CCR_NIS = rep(c(0.25, 0.30), each = 12L)
)
keys <- c("YEAR", "HOSP_NIS")
stopifnot(!anyNA(ccr[keys]), !anyDuplicated(ccr[keys]))
charges <- dplyr::left_join(
  charges, ccr, by = keys, relationship = "many-to-one", na_matches = "never"
)
```

Each discharge can match at most one ratio. The left join keeps the
unmatched year in the analysis data so its missing costs can be reported.

## Convert charges to costs

`nis_cost()` multiplies charges by `CCR_NIS` to estimate hospital costs.
It expresses both costs and charges in a selected reference-year dollar
using annual CPI-U indices.

```{r cost}
adjusted <- nis_cost(charges, dollars = 2024)
adjusted |>
  dplyr::group_by(YEAR) |>
  dplyr::summarise(missing_costs = sum(is.na(cost_adj)), discharges = dplyr::n())
```

`cost_adj` contains the estimated cost in 2024 dollars and `charges_adj`
contains adjusted charges. These are synthetic amounts intended only to show
the calculation.

## Check provenance

The direct result records the source fields, price index, base year,
multipliers, and invalid input counts.

```{r provenance}
nis_cost_provenance(adjusted)
```

Missing or non-positive CCR values produce missing costs; the corresponding
adjusted charge can still be present. Describe the CCR and inflation choices
when reporting results. Keep the annual CCR source and key coverage with
the analysis record. The provenance accessor records the column used and
the missing or invalid count for the data passed to the calculation.

`nis_design(..., dollars = 2024)` can add these adjusted values to the survey
design when `CCR_NIS` and the selected charge column are kept.

## Common pitfalls

> **Common pitfalls**
>
> - Calling inflation-adjusted charges “costs” without applying a CCR.
> - Treating missing or invalid CCR values as zero cost.
> - Combining `TOTCHG_2023` silently with earlier `TOTCHG`; its definition is
>   different and the package documents the 2023 layout as unverified.
> - Dropping provenance attributes through later data-frame operations before
>   recording the adjustment method.

See [`nis_cost()`](../reference/nis_cost.html),
[`nis_cost_provenance()`](../reference/nis_cost_provenance.html), and
[`nis_design()`](../reference/nis_design.html).
